findings.evidence: specs/publication-queue/spec.md says a queue on a private repository SHALL hold Checks read and Actions read, and that a missing grant SHALL fail the queue run instead of being treated as absent checks. The diff changes no queue or workflow code under template/ or .github/. `grant_token_reads` in scripts/live_scenarios.py:594 patches the copied workflows with `permission-checks/actions: read` only for the sandbox. `check_app_token` only checks that the token step succeeds. Nothing makes a queue fail on unreadable checks. Archiving this delta would put a requirement into accepted specs that no code satisfies. Either the spec should be scoped to the sandbox snapshot, or the behaviour should be implemented and tested.
findings.summary: The publication-queue delta requires queue behaviour that no production code provides. The only implementation is a sandbox-only text rewrite of the snapshot workflows.

findings.evidence: specs/live-lifecycle-sandbox/spec.md: the runner SHALL refuse before any write 'when the configuration names a production resource', and production App keys SHALL NOT be stored in the sandbox. `assert_target` (scripts/live_scenarios.py:541) compares only the repository name, privacy and origin. `check_owner_setup` checks that the secret exists but not which App it belongs to. `coordinator_app` and the backlog binding are never compared with production values.
findings.summary: The isolation requirement is only partly enforced by the target guard.

findings.evidence: `run_scenarios` catches only StepFailure. In `scenario_quick_task`, the direct `run([...git add/commit...])` calls and `pr_state` (via `gh_json`, which raises SandboxError on a transient gh error) propagate to `main`. There the SandboxError becomes a bare 'live scenarios: ...' message with no scenario or step name, and no JSON results. This contradicts the 'fails naming scenario, step and observed state' requirement.
findings.summary: Errors inside a scenario that are not StepFailure abort the run without the per-step report and discard earlier scenario results.

findings.evidence: `run()` builds its error detail as `done.stderr.strip() or done.stdout.strip()`. `finish_until_queued` then checks `QUEUED not in str(error)`. If finish writes any warning to stderr and prints the queued message to stdout, the message is dropped from the detail. The scenario fails as an unexpected error. Subprocesses also run with no timeout, so a hung finish blocks the run until the 3h lease expires.
findings.summary: Detection of the QUEUED handoff can miss the message and fail the scenario.

findings.evidence: `prepare_checkout` now calls `github_git_env(source, Path(root))` for every non-local source. `_git` and `harness_git` call it for fetch and ls-remote of origin. `github_git_env` raises WorkerError 'requires an uncredentialed GitHub HTTPS origin' for ssh, scp-style or GHE hosts. It also raises for a scheme-less relative path that is not a directory under `cwd`. These reads worked before, when only push was restricted.
findings.summary: Clone and fetch now fail for any origin that is not an uncredentialed github.com HTTPS URL or a local path.

findings.evidence: `compose_snapshot` extracts the tree with `git archive head`, but copies `source / 'dev-platform' / 'live-sandbox' / 'overlay'` from the current checkout (scripts/live_scenarios.py:589). With `--head <other commit>` or a dirty tree, the overlay (source contract, checks, CI) may not match the installed scripts. The spec says 'reproducible snapshot of an exact platform head'.
findings.summary: The snapshot is not fully reproducible from the head being installed: the overlay comes from the working tree, not the head.

findings.evidence: tests/test_lifecycle_workers.py `test_private_clone_uses_a_process_scoped_credential` mocks subprocess.run, so no git config is written. It then asserts `assertFalse(config.exists())`, which is trivially true.
findings.summary: The 'no credential in checkout config' assertion cannot fail.

findings.evidence: `apply_settings` skips creation when a ruleset named 'main: sandbox coordinator only' exists. A drifted or edited ruleset therefore persists across 'idempotent' resets. The same method hard-codes `actor_id: 5` for the repository admin role.
findings.summary: The ruleset is created only if one with the same name is absent, and an existing one is never reconciled.
